stories.title: Levent Alpöge claims proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis [pdf]
stories.reason: Alpoge says he and Claude found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis (and GRH); the Lean/Mathlib community has since formally verified it correct.
key_facts: Levent Alpoge announced Nov 20 that working with Claude he found a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, extending to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis and likely the Extended RH.
The Lean/Mathlib community (Lean FRO + Mathlib Initiative) published a joint statement Nov 21 saying the formalized proof is correct.
Verification used Lean's kernel plus independent checkers con-leche and con-ron, which have their own formal soundness proofs back to set theory.
The formalized proof/library is about 17 million lines; mathematicians say distilling the underlying ideas into human-understandable form will take years.
Millennium Prize evaluation rules require 2 years after refereed publication, so no official Clay Institute statement is expected soon regardless of correctness.

stories.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
stories.reason: Amazon says a China-linked actor's autonomous Cairn AI agents found and exploited a real zero-day (CVE-2026-133968, CVSS 9.8) in medical-imaging software and reached root on a university server.
key_facts: Vulnerability: path-traversal flaw in MONAI Label (open-source medical imaging server) <=0.8.5, auth off by default; tracked CVE-2026-133968, CVSS 9.8.
Attackers' Cairn control panel (an open-source autonomous pentest-agent framework) was left exposed with no auth, letting Amazon Threat Intelligence reconstruct the whole operation.
Agents went from mapping the app's API to writing files on the server in about 11 minutes; later wrote a Python reverse shell into sitecustomize.py to get root.
Activity ran Sept 8-10, 2026 against East Asian university targets; attribution to a China-linked actor is 'moderate confidence' based on language/timezone of prompts.
Agents also failed: 16 hours/148 actions against a Redis server, and 30,000+ credential guesses over 6 hours against a GPU server, both unsuccessful.
MONAI maintainers merged a source fix Oct 19 but had not shipped a patched PyPI package (still 0.8.5) as of the report.

stories.title: Frostbite: A new CPU architecture discovered, designed and verified by AI
stories.reason: Architect Labs says AI agent swarms designed Frostbite, a new interaction-net CPU, claiming 4.59x perf/watt over an undisclosed baseline -- concrete numbers and methodology, but pre-silicon and self-reported.
key_facts: Architecture based on interaction nets: computation is local graph rewriting, so parallelism comes from program structure, not threads/caches; language Vine compiles to intermediate form Ivy.
AI agent swarms iterated on compiler, ISA, microarchitecture, RTL, verification and layout; a power model (Arcmodel) was calibrated against RTL estimates to within ~5%.
Claims 4.59x geometric-mean performance-per-watt vs a baseline 'TCPU' across 25 workloads (6.02x on the 10 search-set workloads, 3.83x on 15 held-out workloads) and 8.77x perf/area.
Synthesis at 800MHz, final GDS layout at 500MHz, 0.792mm^2 (quad+4 L3 nodes) at 7nm vs 0.895mm^2 baseline core.
No silicon, FPGA, or independent benchmark exists yet; baseline CPU is anonymized and unreproducible; RTL/ISA/Arcmodel are unreleased (future plan).

stories.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
stories.reason: Researchers demonstrated a lab PoC where a single malicious webpage opened by Meta's Muse agent chained a browser bug and a Linux kernel bug to fully take over the user's cloud machine, including stored chats and credential access.
key_facts: Meta Muse is Meta's personal AI agent (launched Sept 8); each user's agent runs on its own cloud VM, gated by a monitoring layer called Sentinel.
NebuSec: a malicious webpage could exfiltrate and alter a user's conversation history/memories via Muse's browsing with no approval prompt.
Chaining a flaw in Muse's built-in browser with a Linux kernel flaw gave full control of the user's cloud machine, including the credential store and Sentinel itself.
Lab demonstration only, not used against real users; stayed within one user's VM and did not reach the shared host or other users.
NebuSec says Meta fixed all the issues before publication; Meta has not publicly confirmed or commented; no PoC code or exact bug details were published.

stories.title: Restricting AI agents in mobile operating systems platforms from capturing data
stories.reason: Signal will restrict screenshots by default on Android/iOS specifically to stop AI agents built into the OS from reading private chats, and admits the protection is incomplete.
key_facts: Signal's own announcement: restricts screenshots by default to block agentic systems (e.g. iOS 27, some Android builds) that try to read chats on-screen.
Signal says the feature can detect an AI assistant attempting to read the Signal app and explicitly calls the protection 'incomplete.'
This is a defensive move against a new OS-level threat model: AI agents with screen/accessibility access reading data out of other apps, not just malware.

stories.title: Yamz-Labs/kyojin
stories.reason: Kyojin is a new open-source OpenAI-compatible inference engine (built on ExLlamaV3) for running 100GB-class open models on a single desktop -- AMD Strix Halo, RTX, or Mac -- with published per-model throughput numbers.
key_facts: Runs GLM-5.3-Flash (100.1GB), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (95.4GB) and MiMo-V2.6-Flash-MOPD (105GB) on a 128GB AMD Strix Halo box via ROCm; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (184.7GB) on Mac Studio or Strix SSD tier.
Reports decode/prefill tok/s at 8K context: GLM-5.3-Flash 32/633, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 53/1576, Qwen3.8-27B on RTX 3090 75/1621, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Mac Studio M5 Ultra 62/3001.
Context limits reported up to 983K tokens (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Mac) and 500K (GLM-5.3-Flash); a 763B model on one 128GB machine runs experimentally at 5-11 tok/s.
All numbers are the maintainers' own, unverified independently; MIT licensed, OpenAI-compatible API.

stories.title: The stochastic parrots have apparently proved the Riemann Hypothesis
stories.reason: Scott Aaronson flips from skeptical to convinced on the Claude/Alpoge RH proof once a Lean certificate landed, and argues Lean-verified AI math claims now carry higher assurance than typical journal papers.
key_facts: Aaronson: 'The proof is correct' -- his update came specifically because the proof has an independent Lean certificate checked by con-leche, which is itself formally verified back to set-theory axioms.
He notes no AI math result with a Lean certificate has yet been retracted, while several uncertified ones have.
He separates 'verified' from 'understood': the formalized proof is ~17M lines, and mathematicians will need years to distill and explain the actual ideas.
His remaining worry: future AI systems could reward-hack soundness gaps in proof assistants themselves, so he wants Lean's foundations hardened further.
